function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

Here are a few options you can try: | Option | How to run it | What you’ll see | |--------|---------------|-----------------| | **Web UI** | Open a browser and go to (or ) | A quick test that shows download, upload, and ping. | | **Command line – `speedtest-cli`** | 1. Open PowerShell or Command Prompt.
2. Run `speedtest-cli` (or `speedtest` if you have the newer package). | Text output with download, upload, and ping. | | **Install `speedtest-cli` via pip** | ```powershell\npip install speedtest-cli\nspeedtest-cli\n``` | Same as above. | | **Use PowerShell’s built‑in web request (very basic)** | ```powershell\n(New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/speedtest-cli/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py') | python -\n``` | Runs the Python script directly; shows speeds. | ### Quick command‑line test (if you have Python) If you already have Python installed, you can run a one‑liner that pulls the script from GitHub and executes it: ```powershell powershell -Command "(New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/speedtest-cli/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py') | python -" ``` This will give you a text report similar to: ``` Testing download speed... Testing upload speed... Download: 85.23 Mbit/s Upload: 12.45 Mbit/s Ping: 24.7 ms ``` ### If you prefer a GUI Just open your browser and visit . Click “Go” and wait a few seconds. The page will display your download and upload speeds along with ping. --- **Tip:** If you’re on a corporate or university network, sometimes the speed test may be throttled or blocked. In that case, try a different test site or ask your IT department for help. Let me know if you’d like me to run a command for you (e.g., `speedtest-cli`) and I can guide you through the steps!
